content: Pedro Alborna Soler was the first Spanish individual to earn the title of Doctor of Chiropractic (DC). At the age of 30, he enrolled in the Palmer School of Chiropractic and Infirmary on August 2, 1916. At the time of his enrollment, he listed his home address as Springfield, Massachusetts. He was assigned matriculation number 2958 and paid $250 for a 12-month course of study. Before attending Palmer, his occupation was listed as a steward in a hotel. His enrollment at Palmer was facilitated by a referral from Dr. Cary. On September 28, 1916, Pedro transitioned to the 36-month program that was being offered at the time. However, following a decision by the faculty, he was allowed to return to the 12-month program, from which he graduated on November 11, 1917. It was noted that he retained eligibility to complete the longer program if he chose to do so in the future. During his studies, he achieved 17 grades of A, 7 grades of B, and 4 grades of C. After his graduation, Pedro moved to Spain to practice chiropractic. He became the first chiropractor to establish a practice in Spain, specifically in Plaza Ledesma, Barcelona.
